new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level only: every Lakes Plain language (Rasawa included in the 20 languages of the study) is described as tonal with at least H and L; stress is said not to have been found contrastive in any Lakes Plain language. Nothing states where stress falls in Rasawa, and the Rasawa data behind this is a single 1987 survey word list on which stress was not marked.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author notes only a few of the original word lists marked stress at all.
new_statements.domain_note: NOT a Rasawa-specific statement: a blanket remark in a comparative reconstruction paper about all Lakes Plain languages, based for Rasawa on L. Jones's February 1987 survey word list (village Rasawa), which Clouse reproduces without stress or tone marks. Word-list citation forms only.
new_statements.identity_note: Rasawa = rasa1243 [rac], Far West Lakes Plain, sister of Saponi (Clouse 1997 lexicostatistics: Rasawa shares about half its basic vocabulary with Saponi). Clouse's Rasawa word list was elicited in Rasawa village (Feb 1987, L. Jones); Ethnologue 19 places the language in 2 villages at the Rombak river mouth, Waropen Bawah. No dialect issue; the only 'description' covering it is a family-level comparative paper, not a Rasawa-specific one.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Precursor of Clouse 1997 with the same Rasawa passages (abbreviations, tree, consonant clusters, PFW reflexes Table 5, Rasawa de-ye 'water'). Sec.10 Tone Typology (printed pp.19-20): 'tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plains languages.. All the modern languages have at least high and low tone.' No comparative word-list appendix and no mention of stress anywhere in the article. Reference list confirms Jones 1987 survey ms, Clouse 1992 Wapoga River survey ms, Holster & Bouwman 1986 Waropen Bawah survey ms (all unpublished SIL Jayapura).
